paper.title: Blind Exploration and Exploitation of Stochastic Experts

settings.name_in_paper: Blind exploration and exploitation (BEE) of stochastic experts
unmapped: Arms are M stochastic experts giving binary opinions on a hidden uniformly random binary state Y(t); the reward 1(X_i(t)=Y(t)) is never observed (unsupervised/blind); learner observes only opinions of all consulted experts (multiple experts consulted per task) and uses agreement with a peer committee's majority vote as surrogate reward
Opinions conditionally independent given the state; competences p_i > 1/2 for all experts
settings.definition_quote: The first objective of the BEE problem is to identify the best expert in a population while actively consulting members of that group on tasks that change from one consultation to another. ... \tilde{R}_T = \max_{i\in[M]} p_i - \frac{1}{T}\expt{\sum_{t=1}^{T} \ind{X_{I_t}(t)=Y(t)}}.

settings.name_in_paper: Blind exploration and exploitation (BEE) of stochastic experts (known horizon, MOSS)
unmapped: Arms are M stochastic experts giving binary opinions on a hidden uniformly random binary state; reward never observed; surrogate reward is agreement with a peer committee's majority vote
Opinions conditionally independent given the state; competences p_i > 1/2 for all experts

source.label: main_lemma
source.quote: Let the player designate a subset of experts $\comm{}\subset[M]$ as peers prior to exploration and exploitation and consult them for every task ... Then, the regret of a BEE algorithm that picks $I_t = \argmax_{i\in[M]\setminus\comm{}}\Psi_i(t)$ ... is bounded by: $\tilde{R}_{T}\leq C\frac{ \Phi}{2p_{\comm{}}-1}$, where the constant $C=10$ for UCB1, $C=\nicefrac{1}{2}$ for KL-UCB and IMED.

results.notes: Paper's regret is normalized by T; expression multiplied by T. Derived as corollary of Audibert & Bubeck UCB bound via Proposition 1 (gaps shrink by factor 2p_C-1). Note derivation would naturally give (2p_C-1) in the denominator applied to gaps; recorded as stated.
